title: Existence of the normalized degreewise evaluation map
statement: For any commutative ring A and cochain complexes P,Q on the one-object bottom-topology ringed site [def-pc-perfect-rhom-base-change-map], and any integer n, there exists a morphism from the degree n of Tot(Hom(P,A[0]) tensor Q) to Hom(P,Q)^n satisfying the signed evaluation normalization [lem-pc-perfect-ring-hom-tensor-degree-condition]. No boundedness, finiteness, or projectivity hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Tag 0A6A, lemma-base-change-RHom, clause (1), expanded chain-level evaluation; Tag 0ATK, lemma-base-change-evaluation-map, clause (1)

proof.text: At the unique object, evaluate the degree-r dual by the actual Hom projection at -r and the canonical isomorphism A[0]^(-r+r) to A. Package this evaluation as a curried A-linear map. Extend a pointwise linear map to the one-object presheaves, then restrict to the slice; this gives the explicit linear map from module Homs to sections of the internal sheaf Hom. Compose with Mathlib LinearMap.smulRightₗ and multiply the evaluation by the integer sign (r*s).negOnePow. This constructs a bilinear family with values in internalHom(P^(-r),Q^s). Every site object and every restriction morphism is the unique one, so the family is natural. The linearity equations are proved by eliminating the slice object and its unique arrow, without a duplicate slice-uniqueness declaration.

Apply the proved sheaf tensor bilinear universal property to the signed family. Its pure-tensor formula is exactly the normalization using perfectRingTensorSectionMap. Evaluate at the identity slice object and use the explicit pointwise construction to obtain the signed rank-one formula. This constructs the pairing from each (r,s) sheaf tensor summand into internalHom(P^(-r),Q^s), without finiteness assumptions.

For r+s=n, place this pairing in the Hom product coordinate p=-r, with the equality transport from Q^s to Q^(-r+n), and put zero in all other coordinates. Use the specified limiting fan of homComplex_isLimit (the generic product-property API of homComplex_exists), with precisely ringHomComplexProjection, to lift this family. Fan.IsLimit.fac gives its composite with every projection.

Assemble the maps of the tensor summands by HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctorDesc. The coproduct and product factorization identities give the off-diagonal zero formula. On the diagonal, substitution proves that evaluation after transporting the internal Hom target is transport after evaluation; combine this with the summand pure-tensor formula to prove the exact existing normalization predicate. Neither the construction nor these equations require boundedness, projectivity, finite generation, or a nonzero ring.
